title: The king’s proclamation
summary: The king of the Lamanites sends a proclamation among his people protecting Ammon, Aaron, Omner, Himni, and their preaching brethren. His decree permits them access to houses, temples, and sanctuaries. The king and his household have been converted unto the Lord.

explicit_facts.text: The king of the Lamanites sent a proclamation among all his people.
The proclamation forbade his people from laying hands on Ammon, Aaron, Omner, Himni, or their preaching brethren.
His decree forbade binding, imprisoning, spitting upon, smiting, expelling from synagogues, scourging, or casting stones at them, and allowed them access to houses, temples, and sanctuaries.
The king and all his household had been converted unto the Lord.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The proclamation may be represented visually without specifying how it was delivered.
unspecified_visual_details: The proclamation’s physical form and method of delivery.

narration.text: the king of the Lamanites sent a proclamation among all his people
that the word of God might have no obstruction

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The prohibited acts are terms of the decree, not events occurring in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict attacks, punishments, or confrontations as occurring.
Do not depict Ammon, Aaron, Omner, Himni, or their brethren as physically present solely because the proclamation names them.
Do not identify the king as Lamoni’s father; these verses do not do so.

title: Preaching throughout the land
summary: After the king sent forth a proclamation, Aaron and his brethren went from city to city and between houses of worship, establishing churches and consecrating priests and teachers among the Lamanites. Thousands came to know the Lord, believed in the traditions of the Nephites, and were taught records and prophecies. Those converted through the preaching of Ammon and his brethren did not fall away.

explicit_facts.text: The king had sent forth a proclamation before Aaron and his brethren went forth.
Aaron and his brethren went from city to city and from one house of worship to another, establishing churches and consecrating priests and teachers among the Lamanites.
Thousands were brought to the knowledge of the Lord and to believe in the traditions of the Nephites; they were taught records and prophecies.
The Lamanites who believed and were converted through the preaching of Ammon and his brethren never fell away.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A gathering of listeners could accompany the described preaching and teaching.
unspecified_visual_details: Which of Aaron's brethren were present at any particular stop.
The appearance of the cities, houses of worship, records, and people.

narration.text: Aaron and his brethren went forth from city to city
thousands were brought to the knowledge of the Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Ammon is named in the retrospective account of preaching; the verses do not place him at a particular stop with Aaron.
The reference to miracles does not describe a specific visible miracle.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify Aaron's unnamed brethren as Omner or Himni.
Do not depict a specific miracle or portray the converts' lifelong faithfulness as a single visible event.

title: Weapons laid down
summary: The converted Lamanites become a righteous people and lay down their weapons of rebellion, no longer fighting against God or their brethren.

explicit_facts.text: The converted people laid down their weapons and no longer fought against God or their brethren.

reasonable_visual_inferences: People setting weapons down is a direct visual rendering of the stated action.
unspecified_visual_details: The people involved, the weapons' types, and the precise location.

narration.text: they did lay down the weapons of their rebellion

prohibited_inventions: Do not show a battle; none occurs in this verse.

title: Converted Lamanite communities
summary: The account identifies Lamanites converted to the Lord in Ishmael, Middoni, Nephi, Shilom, Shemlon, Lemuel, and Shimnilom. They laid down their weapons of war.

explicit_facts.text: The people of the Lamanites in the land of Ishmael were among those converted to the Lord.
The people of the Lamanites in the land of Middoni were among those converted to the Lord.
The people of the Lamanites in the city of Nephi were among those converted to the Lord.
The people of the Lamanites in the land of Shilom, the land of Shemlon, the city of Lemuel, and the city of Shimnilom were among those converted to the Lord.
Those identified laid down all their weapons of war; they were all Lamanites.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The named communities may be shown separately rather than gathered in one place.
Lamanites may be shown laying down weapons, without depicting injury.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance and geography of the named places.
The people's clothing and physical appearance.
The types and appearance of the weapons.

narration.text: Now, these are they who were converted unto the Lord:
and these are they that laid down the weapons of their rebellion, yea, all their weapons of war;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The list identifies communities; it does not establish that their people gathered together at one moment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not combine the named lands and cities into one physical location or simultaneous gathering.
Do not invent speakers, dialogue, individual identities, or additional events.

title: Those who did not convert
summary: Only one Amalekite converted, and no Amulonites converted. They hardened their hearts and the hearts of Lamanites where they lived. The narrator has named the cities where Lamanites repented and converted.
locations: The part of the land where the Amalekites and Amulonites dwelt
The previously named cities of the Lamanites

explicit_facts.text: The Amalekites were not converted except for one; no Amulonites were converted.
They hardened their own hearts and the hearts of Lamanites in the part of the land where they dwelt, including their villages and cities.
Mormon says the cities of the Lamanites where people repented, came to the knowledge of the truth, and converted have been named.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A visual contrast may distinguish the resistant groups from the previously named converted cities without placing them together in a new event.
unspecified_visual_details: The identity of the one converted Amalekite
The appearance of the people and settlements
The exact locations of the villages and cities

narration.text: And the Amalekites were not converted, save only one; neither were any of the Amulonites; but they did harden their hearts, and also the hearts of the Lamanites in that part of the land wheresoever they dwelt, yea, and all their villages and all their cities.
Therefore, we have named all the cities of the Lamanites

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Mormon is the first-person narrator, not a speaker in a depicted exchange.
Hardening hearts is figurative, not a visible physical change.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict hearts physically changing.
Do not invent a confrontation, dialogue, or an identity for the one converted Amalekite.
Do not place the previously named converted communities in a new shared event with these groups.

title: Choosing a new name
summary: The king and those who were converted desire a name to distinguish themselves from their brethren. The king consults Aaron and many of their priests. They take the name Anti-Nephi-Lehies and are no longer called Lamanites.

explicit_facts.text: The king and those who were converted wanted a name to distinguish themselves from their brethren.
The king consulted Aaron and many of their priests about the name.
They were called Anti-Nephi-Lehies and were no longer called Lamanites.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The king, Aaron, and priests may be shown together during the consultation.
unspecified_visual_details: The location and participants’ appearances are not specified.
The words exchanged during the consultation are not supplied.

narration.text: And it came to pass that they called their names Anti-Nephi-Lehies;

prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the king beyond the supplied verses.
Do not invent dialogue for the consultation.

title: Industry and friendship
summary: The Anti-Nephi-Lehies become industrious and friendly with the Nephites, open correspondence with them, and are no longer followed by the curse of God.

explicit_facts.text: The Anti-Nephi-Lehies became industrious, were friendly with the Nephites, and opened correspondence with them.
The curse of God no longer followed them.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A written exchange may represent the correspondence, though the text does not specify its form.
unspecified_visual_details: The nature of their work, the form of correspondence, and whether any Nephites are physically present.

narration.text: they did open a correspondence with them

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The curse is narrated as no longer following them, without a visible manifestation described.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a specific curse or its removal as a supernatural visual event.
